title: Guidelines for hardware-focused articles
abstract:
Guidelines for hardware-focused articles
Jason E. Hein
*a and Joshua Schrier
*b
In this editorial, we set expectations and requirements for hardware-focused articles to Digital Discovery.
We discuss the four criteria that should be addressed by authors and reviewers: (1) relevance to the
digitalization of chemical research (broadly deﬁned); (2) comparative analysis of the hardware to existing
alternatives; (3) replicability and modiﬁcation of the design; (4) instructions for operation and safety.

mous labs is a challenging yet rewarding
interdisciplinary endeavor. The integra-
tion, instrumentation, and oen, the
innovative design and construction of
hardware, are crucial stepping stones in
this journey. However, a palpable chal-
lenge looms in the form of a glaring
absence
of
“mainstream”
materials-
science or chemistry journals that cater
to researchers engrossed in autonomous
research
integration,
instrumentation,
and hardware. Too oen, the description
of discovery-enabling hardware is teth-
ered to a larger scientic demonstration
project.
This
inadvertently
creates
a bottleneck, hindering the ow of inno-
vation and collaborative eﬀorts essential
for advancing this domain.
The
interdisciplinary
expansion
of
digital transformation within chemical
and material science has necessitated
a greater emphasis on articles dedicated
to
hardware
advancements.
Digital
Discovery
has
witnessed
a
surge
in
submissions of hardware articles, along-
side an inux of author and reviewer
queries regarding the journal’s expecta-
tions in this domain. In this editorial we
address those questions and set expecta-
tions and requirements for submissions
describing discovery-enabling hardware.

methods.value: Setting expectations and requirements for hardware-focused articles in Digital Discovery, focusing on four criteria: relevance, comparative analysis, replicability, and operation and safety.

problems.value: Lack of a 'mainstream' materials-science or chemistry journal catering to researchers focused on autonomous research integration, instrumentation, and hardware.

hypotheses.value: Establishing a peer-reviewed forum for hardware-focused articles will assure readers of the relevance, capability, feasibility, and usability of the hardware in a scientific setting and recognize genuine scholarly contributions in this emerging field.

evidence.value: The surge in submissions of hardware articles and influx of author and reviewer queries regarding the journal’s expectations in this domain.

conclusions.value: Digital Discovery will specialize in open-source scientific instrumentation that propels digitalization, automation, and autonomy in chemistry, materials research, and biotechnology.

mechanisms.value: Setting expectations and requirements for submissions

outcomes.value: Assurance of relevance, capability, feasibility, and usability of hardware
Promotion of digitalization, automation, and autonomy in scientific research

provenance.cross_sdl_notes: The editorial outlines the criteria and expectations for hardware-focused articles in Digital Discovery but does not explicitly detail failed attempts or a detailed exploration narrative.

notes: Full-text or LLM extraction is needed for reliable hardware/method coverage.
